title: A one-dimensional activated random walk is explosive above the critical density and not explosive below it
author: Nicolas Forien, Christopher Hoffman, Tobias Johnson, Josh Meisel, Jacob Richey and Leonardo T. Rolla
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: original Theorem 1.1 of the article (source label thm:explosive, source0.tex lines 267--274), the main result of the paper: a one-dimensional activated random walk with ergodic initial configuration of density $\rho$ is almost surely explosive above the critical density $\rho_c$ and almost surely not explosive below it. It is delivered with the authors' own complete 15-line proof at source0.tex lines 626--640. H2: the proof is short but it is the synthesis of the whole paper rather than a qualifying examination exercise. The solver must combine two different mechanisms: below criticality, fixation of the process started with all particles active, quoted from the literature, together with the monotonicity of the odometer under the activation of particles; above criticality, the ergodic theorem with the delivered Proposition 2.5 to show that stabilizing after waking all particles at nonvacant sites visits all of $\mathbb{Z}$ with positive probability, then the delivered Lemma 2.1 to see that the odometer is unchanged by preemptively waking every particle, and finally the quoted infinite-odometer theorem to rule out fixation. Recognising and assembling that dichotomy, with the correct monotonicity and preemptive-waking inputs, is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying level.
